questions.question: You are creating an AI agent in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service. Which THREE components make up the agent definition?

options.text: A model deployment
options.why: Correct. The model reads requests, reasons and decides which actions to take.

options.text: Instructions
options.why: Correct. Instructions define the agent's role, rules and tone.

options.text: Tools
options.why: Correct. Tools such as file search, code interpreter or function calling let the agent retrieve data and take actions.

options.text: A virtual network gateway
options.why: A virtual network gateway is a networking resource and is not part of an agent definition.

options.text: A content delivery network profile
options.why: A content delivery network caches web content and is not part of an agent definition.

questions.explanation: An agent combines a model, instructions and tools so that it can plan and act toward a goal.

questions.question: A marketing team needs an AI solution that writes three alternative product descriptions from a short list of product features. The solution does not need to access any other systems. Which approach is the most appropriate?

options.text: A generative AI model called with a prompt
options.why: Correct. Creating new text from a prompt is a generative AI task that does not require tools.

options.text: A multi-agent system with an orchestrator
options.why: A multi-agent system adds unnecessary cost and complexity for a single content-generation task.

options.text: A sentiment analysis model
options.why: Sentiment analysis classifies existing text and does not write new descriptions.

options.text: A speech-to-text model
options.why: Speech to text converts audio to text. The input is a list of features.

questions.explanation: When the task is only to create new content and no tools or actions are needed, a single call to a generative model is sufficient.

questions.question: Which statement describes how an AI agent completes a task that requires information from an external system?

options.text: The agent relies only on the data used to train its model
options.why: Training data does not contain current information from external systems.

options.text: The agent plans a step, calls a tool, observes the result and decides the next step
options.why: Correct. Agents repeat a plan, act and observe loop until they can complete the task.

options.text: The agent retrains its model each time a user sends a request
options.why: Agents do not retrain the underlying model for each request.

options.text: The agent forwards every request to a human operator
options.why: Agents can include human approval steps, but they complete tasks by using tools rather than forwarding every request.

questions.explanation: An agent uses tools to retrieve information or take actions, observes the results and continues until the goal is met.

questions.scenario: A company has a single support agent that handles billing, shipping and returns. Its instructions have grown long and it often selects the wrong tool.
questions.question: Which design change addresses this problem?

options.text: Increase the temperature of the agent's model
options.why: A higher temperature increases randomness and is likely to make tool selection less reliable.

options.text: Remove all tools from the agent
options.why: Without tools the agent cannot complete billing, shipping or return tasks.

options.text: Split the work into specialist agents coordinated by an orchestrator
options.why: Correct. A multi-agent design gives each agent a narrow job and a small set of tools, which improves reliability.

options.text: Replace the agent with a speech synthesis model
options.why: Speech synthesis converts text to audio and cannot handle support tasks.

questions.explanation: Multi-agent systems split a large job across specialist agents, each with focused instructions and tools, coordinated by an orchestrator or workflow.

questions.question: Generative AI language models produce text by repeatedly performing which operation?

options.text: Looking up the complete answer in a database of stored responses
options.why: Language models do not retrieve pre-written answers from a database of responses.

options.text: Predicting the next token based on the preceding tokens
options.why: Correct. Language models generate output one token at a time, each predicted from the context so far.

options.text: Translating the prompt into a programming language
options.why: Language models do not translate every prompt into code to answer it.

options.text: Classifying the prompt as positive or negative
options.why: That describes sentiment analysis, not text generation.

questions.explanation: Generative language models are trained to predict the next token, and they build a response by repeating that prediction.
